title: GuardAgent: Safeguard LLM Agents via Knowledge-Enabled Reasoning
evidence: Guard LLM gets safety requests + target-agent spec + 'user inputs to the target agent, along with associated outputs and logs' (agent reasoning, generated code, predicted action; no raw web/DB content) => DERIVED; LLM generates guardrail code at inference that an external engine executes deterministically (SEP;RULE, policy from human-written NL requests => LLM); 'the actions of the target agent with safety violations will be denied by GuardAgent' (admit if O_l=0, deny if O_l=1) => A pre. Threat = misuse by unauthorized personnel (access-control/rule violation), no formal adversary. adaptive=0: no attack/jailbreak/evasion evaluation found, test sets are natural rule-violating cases. Metrics: LPA >98% EICU-AC, >83% Mind2Web-SC; FRA 100%; time ~31.9s/30.0s; prompt ~571/1265 words; no explicit FPR (LPP/LPR only). Backbones GPT-4, Llama3-70B, Llama3.1-70B, Llama3.3-70B. adversarial=Y is a borderline call (unauthorized-user misuse); N/NA if strict.

title: Constitutional Black-Box Monitoring for Scheming in LLM Agents
evidence: Monitor = prompted LLM (Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT 5.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro); input 'a trajectory T - with the agent's internal reasoning removed - containing user queries, tool calls, and tool outputs' => RAW (tool outputs). 'we optimize and evaluate monitors on completed agent trajectories for use in asynchronous and offline settings' => post-hoc detection, scalar suspicion score 1-10 (flag/allow threshold). Adversary = scheming/misaligned agent given a secret side task (side task removed from transcript); agent not told about the monitor; paper only optimizes the monitor prompts (grid search, human refinement, DSPy GEPA/MIPROv2; pilot SFT of Kimi K2.6) and does not attack the monitor => adaptive 0. pAUROC over FPR in [0,0.20], balanced 50:50 benign/scheming test (7,500 traj); no FPR at fixed threshold, no cost/latency, no main-task utility.

title: Privacy in Action: Towards Realistic Privacy Mitigation and Evaluation for LLM-Powered Agents
evidence: PrivacyChecker (prompting, no training): LLM 'enumerate[s] each contextual information flow implied by the user query, tool outputs, and accumulated history', gives Yes/No per flow; flows marked No are 'exclu[ded] or abstract[ed]' in the final message => modify. Main variant = same agent LLM in one prompt (SELF); MCP variants: system prompt, tool-embedded, and standalone tool send_privacy_check that 'receives both the drafted message and the action trajectory' (SEP) with 'must obtain approval by invoking send_privacy_check before calling gmail_send_message' => pre-send. Judge sees tool outputs (emails/Notion) => RAW. Threat: inadvertent leakage; limitation sentence 'Adversarial scenarios, such as memory poisoning or contextual ambiguity could disrupt flow extraction or privacy judgment' => N/NA. Backbones: GPT-4o, GPT-4.5, o1, Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-14B, DeepSeek-R1 (+ o3 on Live) =7. Utility: helpfulness 2.69->2.45 (GPT-4o); leak rate 33.06%->8.32%. No latency/token/cost reported; no FPR/over-sanitization metric beyond helpfulness-conditioned leak rate.

title: OS-Sentinel: Towards Safety-Enhanced Mobile GUI Agents via Hybrid Validation in Realistic Workflows
evidence: Hybrid = Formal Verifier (hand-crafted rules: SHA256 system-state integrity, 'curated lexicon of sensitive terms', regex for emails/passwords/cards over system state trace + UI text) + VLM Contextual Judge J(o_t,a_t) over raw screenshots/accessibility trees (windows of steps in 'consecutive'/'sampled' mode) => RAW (app UI content). Primarily post-hoc trajectory-level detection and step-level localization with 'delay-penalized scoring'; step-level judge is described as 'enabling real-time intervention as a safety guard' but this is potential, evaluated on completed trajectories; 'Guard-then-Ask' (human intervention) is future work => A post, hitl '-'. Threat: 'threats can originate not only from malicious user intent, but also from unintended agent-side behaviors' (taxonomy incl. prompt injection 5.9%) => adversarial Y but no evasion/adaptive evaluation (adaptive 0). Fusion strict (OR) / consensus (AND). Backbones: gpt-oss-120B, Qwen2.5-VL-7B, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Claude-3.7-Sonnet, Claude-4.5-Sonnet. Metrics Accuracy/F1 only (no FPR; qualitative FP analysis). 'average latency of 66ms per detection'. No agent task-success measurement with the monitor.

title: MCP-Guard: A Multi-Stage Defense-in-Depth Framework for Securing Model Context Protocol in Agentic AI
evidence: 'functions as a proxy-based security middleware interposed between the MCP Host and Server' intercepting tool calls => A pre. Stage I six regex detectors (hand-written, origin undisclosed; ~1.8ms) => RULE/MAN; Stage II fine-tuned multilingual E5 classifier (ML; ambiguous 0.45<P<0.55 escalates; 55.1ms); Stage III zero-shot LLM 'Security Compliance Auditor' with prompt 'Analyze the following MCP tool call for adversarial intent' on '[Tool]: {name}; [Args]: {json_params}' (the 'raw tool invocation payload'); output {safe,unsafe,uncertain}, uncertain falls back to Stage II threshold. judge_input RAW is an inference: paper does not state whether description/inputSchema text is included, but attack samples are embedded 'in valid MCP fields (e.g., description, inputSchema)' (tool poisoning); if only name+args then DERIVED. Threat: tool poisoning, shadowing, RADE, injection. No adaptive/evasion evaluation (Box 1 are illustrative cases; limitations only mention protocol evolution) => 0. Test 5,258 (2,153 adv/3,105 benign), precision/recall/F1 only (no FPR); no end-to-end agent utility; latency 455.9ms avg pipeline (505.9ms with GPT-4o-mini). 8 Stage III LLMs: GPT-4o-mini, DeepSeek-chat, Mistral-7B, Qwen2.5-0.5B, Llama-3-8B, TinyLlama-1.1B, Llama-2-13B, Gemma-7B. Policy = regex+training data, no external standard.

title: Goal-Aware Identification and Rectification of Misinformation in Multi-Agent Systems
evidence: ARGUS: a distinct corrective LLM agent a_cor 'when a message m flows through one of the critical channels identified by our localization mechanism ... will activate a multistage process of in-depth analysis and intervention' (CoT identification + persuasive rectification); outputs 'revised, factually accurate version of the message' (modify, not block); channels chosen by graph centrality + goal relevance. Input = intercepted inter-agent messages / 'complete dialogue logs of the MAS from round r' (carry RAG/tool-injected content) => RAW; no ground-truth of injected content, task goal inferred. Threat: covert misinformation injected via prompt injection, RAG poisoning, tool injection; attack methods are static, no defense-aware attacker => adaptive 0. Utility: TSR 87.47% vanilla -> 67.70% under attack, ARGUS ~+10.33% TSR; MT -28.17% (PI), -20.38% (RAG), -35.95% (TI). Limitation: 'efficiency of ARGUS requires further consideration ... computational overhead' but no token/latency numbers; no FPR / no clean-with-defense run. Backbones GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, Gemini-2.0-flash; baselines Self-Check, G-Safeguard.

title: MemPot: Defend Against Memory Extraction Attack with Optimized Honeypots
evidence: Honeypot documents optimized (InfoNCE, then scorer-guided LLM decoding/embedding inversion, offline) are injected into memory; online detector = Wald SPRT over per-round log-likelihood ratios computed from retrieval observations ('query, returned indices and similarity scores') with no LLM at detection time ('zero-online-cost', 'zero online inference latency') => ML, no LLM judge. Memory read stage; 'the block only happens when terminal decision D_t = H1 ... block (e.g. Unanswerable.)'. Threat: extraction attacker with 'the same access privileges as normal users and have no prior knowledge of the defense setting' => adversarial Y, adaptive 0 (IKEA is stealthy/gradual but not defense-aware). Utility: WebShop SR 44.6->43.8, Pokemon QA unchanged; reports TPR@1%FPR and TPR@10%FPR, alpha=beta=0.1; delay 0. One agent backbone (DeepSeek-v3.2), embedding all-mpnet-base-v2, NLI mDeBERTa-v3-base; baselines ControlNet, Agent (LLM) detector, Optimal Seq.

title: ToolSafety: A Comprehensive Dataset for Enhancing Safety in LLM-Based Agent Tool Invocations
evidence: Defense = full-parameter SFT of the agent LLM itself on ToolSafety (LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct); no separate guard => SELF, judge_input '-'. Model refuses before the tool call (direct harm) or after seeing tool output (indirect harm, incl. 'a malicious instruction is hidden within the returned result of a seemingly benign tool call') and across 2-5 step chains; model receives tool outputs => judge_exposed Y. Stage coded I (model hardening) + A (refuse tool invocation). Attacks: jailbreak prompt from Andriushchenko et al. in system message and Worst-of-N repeated sampling (temp 0.7, N=16: 'considered safe only if all n response is safe'; refusal 76.14%->67.61%; jailbreak harm 5.07%->15.00%) are generic, 'not characterized as adaptive' / not designed against the defense => adaptive 0. Utility: BFCL helpfulness ~45%; over-refusal 14.77% -> 2.27% with more data (FPR-like). No inference overhead reported (training on 2 A800 GPUs only). GPT-4o used as scorer.

title: IsolateGPT: An Execution Isolation Architecture for LLM-Based Systems
bench: InjecAgent (1,054 attacks, extended);own:IsolateGPT-system-data-theft attacks (544 new; 1,598 total);own:LangChain functionality (83 queries)
evidence: Hub-and-spoke: per-app process isolation (seccomp, setrlimit, eTLD+1 network limit), non-LLM hub operator mediates inter-spoke communication (ISC), checks predefined request/response formats (app developers define; 'reviewed before the apps are made available on the app store') and creates permission dialogs before app invocation with user data, ISC, and irreversible actions (email, purchase) => A pre, C, P (hub planner LLM plans apps/data needed). Hub's 'assessment of whether a request is unexpected' shown as warning is produced by the hub LLM 'based on the (nonmalicious) user query, (vetted) app descriptions, and (vetted) data available in its memory' (advisory SEP; user decides = HUMAN). judge_input RAW because tool/app descriptions and hub memory (data extracted from app interactions) count as untrusted metadata under the codebook although the paper calls them 'vetted'; policy MIX (LLM plan + user permissions + predefined formats). Threat: malicious apps / content propagation; single-app attacks 'out of our scope'. No adaptive attacker analysis => 0; evaluation 'if query resolution requires user permission, we automatically grant it'. VanillaGPT ASR 20.2% avg; IsolateGPT dialog shown in 7.6% of attacks (100% with warning) => hitl frequency measured only in attack runs. Functionality parity (multi-app 0.76/0.95 same as vanilla). Overhead: 75.73% of queries <30%, p90 1.24x, p95 1.80x latency; cost 1.85x for 10% of queries. GPT-4 only. No FPR.

title: MATE: Policy-Aware Security Auditing for Mobile Agents via Synthesis-Driven Trajectory Learning
evidence: Auditor = fine-tuned small LM (Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B/3B-Instruct) MATE(I, tau, r) over user instruction, normalized ReAct trajectory (Thought, Action, Observation) and a retrieved NL policy (embedding retriever picks top-k from ~1,000 policies); outputs violation label, risk category, rationale. Observations are 'natural-language summaries' made by a trajectory adapter (VLM summarizes screenshots; LLM summarizes filtered A11Y/HTML) => the auditor sees neither raw screenshots nor raw page text => DERIVED. 'MATE currently audits complete trajectories after execution rather than blocking actions step by step during execution' => A post, TRAJ. Threat: 'Attackers have black-box access: They issue arbitrary natural-language instructions and observe the agent's behavior' (+ unintended failures); no evasion/adaptive evaluation => adaptive 0. Metrics Accuracy/F1 only (MATE-3B 95.06% acc / 95.60% F1 on MATEBench-REAL); no precision/FPR table. Latency 0.09s (0.5B), 0.21s (3B) vs GPT-4.1 1.64s, DeepSeek-V3 5.10s. Training data: 140K synthesized trajectories from 158 apps; REAL = 162 trajectories from AutoGLM, Mobile-Agent and own emulator agent. Triage/human review for high-impact cases only suggested, not measured.
